stance.label: Early bull phase · day 3 below the 200-day average

headline: Unrealized profit fell below its 35% floor and 7-day option volatility jumped to 58.5%; day 3 below the 200-day average.
summary: Valuation is now as cold as it gets only near cycle bottoms, but the selling hasn't stopped: relative unrealized profit is 34.1% and only 11.7% of short-term holder supply is in profit. Option buyers are paying up for downside protection, with near-dated volatility 16 points above 3-month; $1.1B of longs were liquidated, yet more accounts are long. The plan hedges after 5 closes below 72,975; today is day 3, earliest on the Nov 16 close.

overview.lead: Price has dropped into the cycle-bottom valuation zone, yet the sellers are still short-term holders and leveraged longs, and no spot buyer has stepped in.
points: Close 64,115, down 6.0% on the day and 15.4% in 7 days, on 1.9× the 20-day average volume, finishing in the lower 17% of the day's range.
Relative unrealized profit is 34.1%, below the 35% floor; since 2012 only 2015, 2018–19, March 2020, 2022 and this June got here (Bitview).
Short-term holders realized 8,462 BTC of losses, 3.8× their profits (CheckOnChain, Nov 14).
Fear & Greed is 13, from 25 a week ago; stablecoins shrank another 1.5% in 7 days.

cycle.lead: The market stage is still bull, day 37, but only 1 supporting light is left after the capital-inflow light went out today.
points: The 200-day average at 72,975 is still rising (72,285 30 days ago); going back to bear needs 30 straight closes below a falling average, which is far off.

1 of 6 lights on, only exchange supply (90-day −0.31%); realized cap's 30-day change went from +0.03% to −0.09%, switching off the inflow light. 12-month momentum, MVRV vs its 1-year mean, short-term holder cost and STH cost vs true market mean are all off.

The weekly trend score is −0.43, week 1 on the negative side, and needs 4 weeks to turn bear; the Dawn Index reads valuation, heat 33.4, week 10 of Daybreak (Nov 13). Neither has moved to Nightfall or bear.
Day 404 after this cycle's top, down 48.6%; the three prior cycles were all below −75% on the same day, and three samples can't set this cycle's timetable.

market.lead: The Sell Pressure Index hit 100 with momentum at 0.08, the first bottom combination under the new formula.
points: This leg is down 26.0% over 54 days from 86,594 on Sep 21, deeper than this cycle's median down leg of −19.4% and in the top quarter of 12 legs.

Since 2012 the bottom combination fired 20 times: higher 30 days later 11 times, median +1.8%, worse than any day's +3.2%; the median drawdown before it ended was −12.2%, and after Aug 2014 price fell another 42%.
The close sits at the 14.8th percentile of the past year, just 0.9% above the 10th-percentile line at 63,547.

deriv.lead: Options switched to panic pricing today while perpetual longs stayed put: $1.1B of long liquidations in a week and open interest barely moved.
points: This section has two findings: 7-day implied vol went from 39.2% to 58.5% and the 25Δ risk reversal is −11.3; open interest is 338,809 BTC, down just 0.5% in 7 days, and funding is back to +4.3%.

On Deribit, aggressively bought put premium beat calls by $56M, puts leading for 17 days; dealers are estimated to be short gamma near 60,000, selling into drops and buying into rallies, which amplifies moves.

The estimated long liquidation band is 61.4–63.2K (2.9% below the close), and estimated liquidations within 5% below are 3× those above, built from Coinalyze's aggregated open interest plus assumed leverage.
The biggest order-book walls are both at 64,000: $196M of asks and $138M of bids, all on Hyperliquid perps.

flows.lead: The capital backdrop turned to outflow today: realized cap's 30-day change went negative while ETFs and stablecoins both kept draining.
points: ETFs −$185M on Nov 13 (CoinMarketCap), the 7th straight outflow day; the 20-day sum is −$2.08B, against −$4.7B and −$5.6B at the deepest points of past stretches, so this one is still shallow.
Stablecoins are $287.0B, down $16.3B in 30 days (DefiLlama); realized cap 30-day −0.09%, and 2018 and 2021 both saw big drops after it hit zero.

The Coinbase premium net of USDT averages −0.015% over 30 days, the 1.6th percentile of 4 years; USDT is at $0.9994 and this month's average so far is the lowest in 50 months, a sign people are converting stablecoins back to dollars.
The estimated ETF holder cost is above the close, which sits 18.8% below it (the low was −26.4% on Jun 30); Polymarket puts a December hike at 94.3%.

onchain.lead: Short-term holder loss-taking is still deepening and long-term holders have started to join, though at half the scale of the June low.
points: This section's finding is relative unrealized profit at 34.1%, below the floor; short-term holder NUPL is −0.18 with only 11.7% of their supply in profit, and the close is at −1.42σ of their cost bands, with −2σ at 58,492.
STH-SOPR is 0.976, below 1 for 9 days and deeper than 0.992 on Oct 30; loss-taking intensity is 4.5, the 5th straight day of concentrated loss-taking (CheckOnChain, Bitview, Nov 14).

Long-term holders realized $1.59B of losses over 7 days, against $3.6B at the Jun 30 low; 42.2% of long-term holder supply is at a loss, and an estimated drop to 61,000 would push that above this cycle's peak.
The 7-day hashrate is 903 EH/s, down 12.1% in a week, and the Puell Multiple is 0.71 (Nov 13); difficulty fell 9.13% on Nov 14 and the Nov 29 adjustment is estimated at another −6.1%.

exit.lead: No exit rule has fired; day 3 closing below the 200-day average, two more days to the hedge condition.
points: Hedge rule: 5 straight closes below the 200-day average at 72,975 → cut 20%, earliest on the Nov 16 close; buy back after 5 closes above or when the MVRV Z 7-day average < 0.5. MVRV Z was 0.46 on Nov 13.
MVRV ÷ prior-cycle peak is 0.456, far from the 0.75 line at 111,935; the top-three indicators read 20 / 17 / 12, all low (Nov 13).

findings.title: Valuation fell into the cycle-bottom zone, but sellers haven't let up
findings.lean_why: This valuation zone has only appeared near cycle bottoms, and price was usually much higher six months later; but selling is still widening, so it can't be called a bottom.
findings.what: BTC's valuation dropped today to a level seen only near cycle bottoms: total unrealized profit is just 34.1% of market cap, below the 35% floor (Bitview, Nov 14).
findings.why: It isn't one indicator: supply in profit fell from 67.2% to 54.2% in a week (Nov 13), only 11.7% of short-term holder supply is in profit with NUPL at −0.18, and the Dawn Index valuation heat of 33.4 is also cold for the past 4 years. The sellers are still speeding up: short-term holders realized 8,462 BTC of losses and STH-SOPR is 0.976, below 1 for 9 days; long-term holders realized $1.59B of losses over 7 days, half the $3.6B at the Jun 30 low. The Sell Pressure Index at 100 with momentum at 0.08 makes the first bottom combination under the new formula.
findings.alt: Relative unrealized profit is per-UTXO, and in the ETF era many coins sit still at custodians, so the floor may be lower than in past cycles; this June's visit lasted only 14 days with a low of 34.5%, and today's 34.1% is already lower. Cold valuation doesn't make sellers stop: after the December 2018 break, it stayed below the floor for 115 days.
findings.history: Breaking 35% clusters near cycle bottoms: all 4 completed episodes since 2012 were higher 180 days later (+39% to +125%), but the 2015 and 2018 ones first fell another 22% and 18%. This June's episode left after 14 days, and price bottomed 4% below the entry. The bottom combination fired 20 times since 2012: higher 30 days later 11 times, median +1.8%, worse than any day's +3.2%.
findings.so: What changed is the valuation backdrop: price is now cycle-level cheap, and on valuation alone there is less room below than above. What didn't change is the selling itself; short-term holders are still taking losses and ETFs and stablecoins are still draining. Neither the market stage nor the exit plan moves on valuation.
findings.next: Within a week, two outcomes: relative unrealized profit stays below 35% while short-term holder losses start to fall, meaning sellers are exhausting at the floor; or a close below the Jun 30 low of 58,532, meaning the floor fails and price may sit below it for a long time, as in 2018.

findings.title: Options flipped to panic pricing in a day, near-dated vol 16 points above 3-month
findings.lean_why: Option buyers are paying up for downside, pricing near-term risk well above longer-dated risk; it's hedging demand, not a call on direction.
findings.what: Options switched to panic pricing today: 7-day implied vol jumped from 39.2% a week ago to 58.5%, 16 points above the 90-day 42.4%, inverting the curve (Deribit, Nov 15 00:17 UTC).
findings.why: Three separate readings point the same way: DVOL went from 39.9 to 47.3; the 30-day 25Δ risk reversal is −11.3 versus −4.5 yesterday, with puts priced further above calls; aggressively bought premium was $64.8M of puts against $8.8M of calls, puts leading for 17 days. Dealers are estimated to be short gamma near 60,000 and must sell into drops, which amplifies a decline. Perpetuals show no such panic, with funding still at +4.3%.
findings.alt: Weekend liquidity is thin and 7-day contracts are few, so a handful of large trades can lift short-dated vol; Nvidia earnings on Nov 17 and FOMC minutes on Nov 18 both fall in the week, so the inversion may be event pricing. Dealer positioning is estimated from trades and covers only about half of open interest.
findings.history: The term structure has been recorded daily only since Nov 6, and this is the 2nd day inverted, so there is no backtest to cite. After the 7 flips in buyer premium, price was higher 30 days later 3 times, median −11.2%, with only one year of data.
findings.so: What changed is option pricing: a big move this week is now bought in and near-dated protection is expensive. What didn't change is direction; an inverted curve only says near-term risk feels large. It comes alongside perpetual longs staying put, so the two markets disagree about risk.
findings.next: If 7-day minus 90-day vol is still above 10 points by the Nov 20 Deribit weekly expiry, the panic is lasting; if the 25Δ risk reversal recovers above −5, it was only weekend hedging.

findings.title: $1.1B of longs liquidated, yet the share of long accounts rose to 76%
findings.lean_why: Flushed longs are replaced right away, leverage never gets lighter, and the fuel for forced selling below is still there.
findings.what: Leveraged longs keep getting flushed and keep coming back: $1.10B of long liquidations in 7 days, open interest down only 0.5%, and the share of long accounts on Binance up to 76.4% (Coinalyze, Nov 14).
findings.why: Broken down, longs are paying the price, 89.6% of all liquidations; but open interest at 338,809 BTC is still in the 97th percentile since 2021, up 7.7% in 30 days while price fell 22%. Funding flipped to −0.9% on the old three-venue basis yesterday and is back to +4.3% on the five-venue weighting today, with Hyperliquid at 10.95%. The estimated long liquidation band sits just 2.9% below the close at 61.4–63.2K, and estimated liquidations within 5% below are 3× those above.
findings.alt: The account share counts accounts, not position size, so small retail accounts buying the dip can lift it; open interest also includes the other leg of basis trades and hedges. The top 2,000 Hyperliquid accounts are actually net short (11,554 vs 7,906 BTC).
findings.history: Long-account share on Binance and Bybit at 72% or more happened 26 times since 2021: higher 90 days later 10 times, median −7.0%, against 53% and +2.1% for any day.
findings.so: Yesterday's "leverage starts to flush" needs a correction today: it was flushed, but replaced just as fast, and total leverage didn't change. That leaves the liquidation band below as a ready-made pile of sell orders; it doesn't change the market stage or the plan.
findings.next: By Nov 20: funding back above 8% means longs keep piling in; the Binance long-account share falling below 65% means retail longs have actually left.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Running on Empty
items.points: BTC near 74K, below short-term holder cost of 75.6K, with only about 35% of short-term supply in profit; true market mean 77.5K; two-thirds of short-term supply sits above price, and the only thick layer below is 62–66K. Stablecoins shrank $14.2B in 30 days; the largest long liquidation band is 59.5–62.6K; holding the June low at 58.5K keeps August's trend reversal intact.
items.meaning: This site's short-term holder supply in profit is now 11.7%; its largest long liquidation cluster at 59.5–62.6K overlaps this site's estimated 61.4–63.2K, and price is at the top edge.

items.title: Bitcoin: Correction or Reset?
items.points: Via media coverage: short-term holder cost 75,717, with BTC below it for 4 days; reclaiming it plus 3 straight ETF inflow days would mark a correction, otherwise a reset; 11 of 14 past breaks were reclaimed within two weeks. Futures open interest 701.9K BTC, up 3.3% while price fell, funding about 11% annualized.
items.meaning: Original not read, so not used as evidence; by its split, a close 14.5% below short-term holder cost and 7 straight ETF outflow days still sit on the "reset" side.
